title: Slowly Changing Dimensions and Versioning: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Slowly Changing Dimensions and Versioning: Visual Guide

1. Overwrite Or Version | customer C42's region change shown under Type 1 and Type 2, with a sale-date slider resolving to the region that applied at sale time | overwriting a dimension rewrites every historical report silently, while a Type 2 version keeps the old row closed rather than deleted

2. The Boundary Instant | two adjacent validity intervals under a half-open convention, an inclusive-both convention, and an accidental gap, with an event at the exact boundary | half-open intervals make every instant belong to exactly one version, inclusive ends double-count boundary events, and gaps leave facts with no dimension at all

3. Early Or Late Binding | a late-arriving correction fired against facts that stored the version key and facts that stored the business key plus event time | early binding needs restatement because stored keys go stale, late binding revises history for free at the cost of a range join on every query

4. The Same Shape, Twice | six SCD Type 2 concepts mapped one-to-one onto their document-versioning equivalents, plus three temporal questions | document versioning is SCD Type 2 with different column names, chunks belong to a document version, and reusing a chunk id across versions breaks caches, citations and labels at once

5. Sufficient History | six attributes classified as keep-every-version, overwrite, wrong-shape, or keep-the-evidence, plus the derived copies a retention policy must reach | history is worth keeping only where a named obligation or decision needs it, and a deleted document still reachable through an embedding is not deleted
